summary: The study describes the preparation of CrOx/Al2O3 catalysts using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) with Cr(acac)3 vapor and air. The Cr loading increased with the number of saturating reactions, and the catalysts were characterized for oxidation state distribution, dispersion, and activity in the dehydrogenation of i-butane. The results indicate that both redox Cr3C and non-redox Cr3C sites are active in the dehydrogenation reaction.
evidence: Atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), a technique relying on saturating gas–solid reactions, was applied in the preparation of CrOx/Al2O3 catalysts using Cr(acac)3 vapor and air as source materials for CrOx. The Cr loading increased from 1.3 to 12.5 wt.% as the number of saturating Cr(acac)3 and air reactions was increased from one to 10. The dehydrogenation activity of the catalysts was studied, and it was proposed that the dehydrogenation reaction uses both reduced Cr6C, i.e. redox Cr3C, and exposed non-redox Cr3C sites.
